transcript.text: My export classification review found that the platform's controlled technical documentation falls under ECCN 3E001. The license must prohibit transfers to embargoed jurisdictions and require an end-user certificate before any controlled technical documentation is transferred. I recorded this in export-control's working folder but had not yet circulated it. These two requirements need to be added to the draft license before tomorrow's executive approval.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for walking through your respective concerns. Let me summarize the three required changes I've identified before I can sign off:

1. From Thomas (chain-of-title): The license must include a specific reservation of the university consortium's continuing non-commercial research rights, as a prior agreement grants those rights and the current worldwide exclusivity would conflict.

2. From Maya (sublicense scope): The sublicense permission must be limited specifically to accredited hospitals, reflecting Helixion's confirmed deployment model.

3. From Owen (export control): The license must prohibit transfers to embargoed jurisdictions and require an end-user certificate before any controlled technical documentation (ECCN 3E001) is transferred.

All three changes need to be incorporated into the draft before it goes to executive approval tomorrow. I will not approve the license as currently drafted. Thomas, please circulate a revised license comment capturing the research-rights reservation. Maya, please add the accredited-hospitals sublicense limitation to the deal-summary spreadsheet. Owen, please circulate your export-control requirements to the drafting team. Once all three amendments are reflected in the draft, I'll complete my sign-off ahead of tomorrow's meeting. Are there any objections to proceeding on this basis?
